---
title: "PHP versions and the JIT"
---

The polyfill supports PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5. CI runs the test suite on each
version on Linux in five modes: without OPcache, with OPcache and no JIT, with
the tracing JIT, with `opcache.jit=1205`, and with `opcache.jit=1235`. On macOS
it runs the OPcache and `opcache.jit=1205` modes. The PHP versions and JIT
modes verification lists the result of every combination with the phit
extension loaded.

## Recommended settings

| PHP | Recommended | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| 8.3 | OPcache without the JIT (PHP 8.3's default) | the tracing JIT; `opcache.jit=1215` and `1235` |
| 8.4 | OPcache without the JIT | the tracing JIT; function JIT with hot-counter triggers, such as `opcache.jit=1235` |
| 8.5 | OPcache without the JIT | function JIT with hot-counter triggers, such as `opcache.jit=1235` |

The settings to avoid are PHP bugs, and they can affect any PHP code, not
only this package. They are recorded here because the polyfill's numerical
loops trigger them.

`Phit\fit_mixed`, `Phit\fit_lmer`, `Phit\fit_logistic_mixed`, and
`Phit\fit_glmer` throw an exception with code 1007 while any JIT compiles the
process, on every PHP version. Their optimizer is the code the JIT has
miscompiled most severely. `Phit\fit_mixed_intercept` uses no optimizer and
still runs.

## PHP 8.4 and 8.5

A function JIT with hot-counter triggers compiles a function while it is
running and enters the compiled code partway through a loop. In that case PHP
can lose the value of a variable that is live across the loop entry
(php-src #24214). The polyfill avoids the patterns that triggered the bug in
its own code, and its full suite passes under `opcache.jit=1235` on both
versions. Because the bug is in PHP, other code paths may still meet it.

On PHP 8.4.26 on GitHub's x86-64 runner, the tracing JIT also miscompiles the
BOBYQA optimizer behind the mixed models without any message. One reference
case ends at a minimum 18% away from the correct one. The failure has not
reproduced on other machines with the same PHP build. PHP 8.5 passes under
the tracing JIT in CI, which was also true of PHP 8.4 before this runner, so
OPcache without the JIT is the only setting recommended on either version.

## PHP 8.3

PHP 8.3 uses an older JIT backend, and that release line receives security
fixes only. With the tracing JIT, one beta-distribution case in the stress
suite returns a value that differs from the extension's in the 12th digit
after certain functions have been compiled. With `opcache.jit=1215` or `1235`,
the PHP process crashes in the test suite. OPcache without the JIT and
`opcache.jit=function` (1205) pass every test, and PHP 8.3 disables the JIT by
default.

PHP 8.3's `round()` first rounds its argument to 15 significant digits, so
`round(0.49999999999999994)` is 1.0 there. The polyfill uses its own exact
rounding, which matches Rust and PHP 8.4.

## Optimizer folding with NaN

OPcache's optimizer rewrites `!($x > 0)` as `$x <= 0`, which differs when `$x`
is NaN. The polyfill writes such conditions so that NaN takes the same branch
as in the extension, with or without OPcache, on all three versions.
